clue.text: Old woman eats ice provided by guide

indicators.note: one who eats takes food inside, so the old woman's word swallows the other piece

parts.note: a crone is a withered old woman

explanation.surface: An elderly lady tucks into an ice cream supplied by her tour guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' puts ICE inside CRONE; 'provided by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicerone is a guide who shows sightseers round antiquities, named after the eloquent Roman orator.

clue.text: One dependant on 'Tom's family tree?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and family is kin; the thing dangles from a willow or hazel

explanation.definitionFit: A catkin is a hanging flower spike on trees such as willow and birch.

clue.text: The effect of eating chemicals

parts.note: read 'eating' as corrosive, chemicals that eat away metal, not chemicals consumed as food

explanation.definitionFit: Corrosion is the gradual wearing away of metal by chemical action, as in rust.

clue.text: Give an encore on the parliamentary stage

definitions.text: Give an encore on the parliamentary stage

parts.words: Give an encore on the parliamentary stage
parts.note: parliament enacts laws, so doing it a second time is an encore there

explanation.definitionFit: To re-enact is to act out again, or to pass a law once more.

clue.text: Those on the "wanted" list

parts.note: not criminals on a police list, but things one requires

explanation.definitionFit: Needs are requirements, things that are wanted.

clue.text: Accident involves his entry into the plan

indicators.note: an entry into something goes inside it, so the jumbled letters go within the plan's word

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area

indicators.note: to involve can mean to entangle or wind up, so the letters of his are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A mishap occurs when some man's name gets written into the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' tangles HIS into ISH, and 'entry into' puts that inside MAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident, a small misfortune.

clue.text: Not out-but not at the wicket

definitions.text: Not out-but not at the wicket

parts.words: Not out-but not at the wicket
parts.note: a cricketer who is not out is still batting, but here simply inside the house rather than at a small gate

explanation.definitionFit: Indoors means inside a building, not outside.

clue.text: It's difficult, with nothing in store

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the word for difficult

parts.note: hard means difficult
O, the shape of zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Things are hard when the larder is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside HARD; 'It's' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stockpile, a hidden stock of valuables or supplies.

clue.text: Cover for blackbirds

parts.note: the nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence has four and twenty blackbirds baked in a pie

explanation.walkthrough: Sing a Song of Sixpence is a well-known English nursery rhyme with blackbirds baked in a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastry lid over a baked pie, under which the rhyme's birds were hidden.

clue.text: The nasty looks of certain customers?

definitions.text: The nasty looks of certain customers?

parts.words: The nasty looks of certain customers?
parts.note: an ugly customer is a dangerous person, and nasty looks here mean an unattractive appearance

explanation.definitionFit: Ugliness is unattractiveness, the quality an ugly customer shows.

clue.text: Sports contest, no abnormality in Man

definitions.meaning: a sports-day event in which pairs run with two legs tied together
the Isle of Man's emblem is a triskelion of three legs, so a race of people with that many legs would be normal there

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, has three running legs on its flag; read 'race' as a people rather than a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports-day race for tied pairs; also, whimsically, a tribe of Manxmen with the island's emblematic triple legs.

clue.text: Pressure is evenly distributed along these lines

definitions.text: Pressure is evenly distributed along these lines

parts.words: Pressure is evenly distributed along these lines
parts.note: on a weather map, lines join places with equal atmospheric pressure

explanation.definitionFit: Isobars are lines on weather charts joining points of equal barometric pressure.

clue.text: No rider can be so tidy

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can be rearranged into another phrase

explanation.surface: A horse with nobody on its back can be kept neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' signals the anagram of NO RIDER; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tidy is neatly arranged, all things in their proper places.

clue.text: Repugnance is stated with some embarrassment

indicators.note: embarrassment suggests confusion, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone admits their revulsion while blushing awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with some embarrassment' scrambles the letters of IS STATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or aversion, close to repugnance.

clue.text: A legal calling — or else!

parts.note: a court summons orders attendance under threat of penalty; calling is a summons, not a profession

explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a writ commanding a witness to attend court, its Latin name meaning under penalty.

clue.text: Rights and lefts taken by disputants

definitions.meaning: the right-hand and left-hand halves of anything
people arguing take positions, opposing camps in a quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: Both right and left are flanks of something; arguers likewise choose opposing camps in a dispute.

clue.text: Last men I'd get to strip anyway!

indicators.note: taken any way you like, the letters fall into a different order

explanation.surface: The final men ready to undress, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' rearranges LAST MEN ID; 'get to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take apart, to strip something down.

clue.text: Pinhead — something small

definitions.meaning: the tiny head of a pin, a very small speck

explanation.definitionFit: Both name a tiny bit of matter: a speck the size of a pin's head, or any minute fragment.

clue.text: They're related to a French type in service in World War II

indicators.note: the French article is placed inside the wartime service's initials

parts.note: ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army corps of the Second World War
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Relatives of a Frenchwoman who served in uniform during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' is a link: a French type in the ATS. 'in' puts UN within ATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Your parents' sisters are relatives by blood, hence family related to you.

clue.text: One thing one can always measure up to

definitions.text: One thing one can always measure up to

parts.words: One thing one can always measure up to
parts.note: everyone is exactly as tall as their own height, so they always match it

explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's natural height.

clue.text: Firm action on stage

definitions.meaning: an actor's incidental movements and gestures in a play

explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a commercial enterprise; in theatre, the term also covers small bits of stage activity by actors.

clue.text: Go on Ann, give it a whirl, cut a figure!

indicators.note: whirling the letters round puts them in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Encouraging Ann to try dancing and show off a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give it a whirl' scrambles GO ON ANN; 'cut a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a geometric figure with nine sides.

clue.text: Divers ways of obtaining these prized possessions?

definitions.text: Divers ways of obtaining these prized possessions?

parts.words: Divers ways of obtaining these prized possessions?
parts.note: divers looks like various, but means people who dive for oysters' gems

explanation.definitionFit: Pearls are prized gems gathered by divers from oyster beds.

clue.text: Rent trouble that may blow over?

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, meaning torn
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Squabbles over unpaid rent that will probably blow over soon.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent whirlwind that can knock buildings flat.

clue.text: Truly this betrays the drunkard

parts.note: a tipsy person trying to say truly slurs it into a countryside word

explanation.definitionFit: Rural means of the countryside; it is famously hard to pronounce when tipsy.

clue.text: Row takes a long time — a family matter

indicators.note: the first piece takes on the second, which follows it

parts.note: a row is a line of things
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: An argument that drags on for ages over a domestic issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry or descent, the family line one belongs to.

clue.text: It's even reversible

indicators.note: the word reads the same either way, so turning it round changes nothing

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something is as good backwards as forwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link; the definition is 'even'.
explanation.definitionFit: Level means flat or equal, the same as even.

clue.text: Sailor certainly gets around

parts.note: a seaman who voyages all the way round the globe really does travel widely

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sails round the world, like Magellan's crew or Drake.

clue.text: She is heard to admit her bias

indicators.note: what follows is spoken aloud, so its sound gives the girl's name

parts.note: a woman admitting a bias would say I lean (one way)

explanation.definitionFit: Eileen is a girl's name, so it can stand for any woman, she.

clue.text: Sports wear for Kipling's fools

definitions.meaning: Kipling's poem The Islanders mocked flannelled fools at the wicket

explanation.walkthrough: Cricketers wear white trousers made of soft wool cloth; Kipling sneered at them as 'flannelled fools'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket whites are traditionally made of the soft woollen cloth, which also names the trousers.
